 Judgment

In these two appeals, the petitioners as well as the KSRTC have challenged the judgment and award dated 11.09.2017 passed in M.V.C.No.493/2016 on the file of the V Additional District and Sessions judge and Addl.MACT., Shivamogga, sitting at Sagar (for short 'the Tribunal').
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.
3. Briefly stated the facts are, the husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioner Nos.2 and 3 by name Bhadrappa @ Bhadra, the deceased on 31.05.2015 after attending a marriage, he was returning to his native in Ambika private bus bearing No.KA-15/2836), at about 4.30 p.m., the bus reached Bhootharayan Temple at Kopparagundi, the passengers since decided to perform pooja, the bus was stopped.
The deceased being the elder member of the group got down from the bus and standing on the left side of the road waiting for alighting of his NC: 2023:KHC:41050 son/petitioner No.2.
At that time, KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-17/F-1712 came from Shivamogga side and hit against the deceased, due to which, deceased sustained injuries.
He was treated at Sahyadri Narayana Multi Specialty Hospital, Shivamogga till 13.06.2015 but he succumbed to the injuries.

sentences.text:
The petitioners have approached the Tribunal seeking grant of compensation of Rs.43,15,000/-
against KSRTC bus as well as Ambika Private bus.
Claim is opposed by the KSRTC including its driver.
After taking the evidence, the Tribunal by the impugned judgment awarded compensation of Rs.8,41,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum.
The Tribunal has fastened the entire liability against the KSRTC to pay the compensation.
Aggrieved by the same, KSRTC has filed M.F.A.No.9366/2017.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement, the petitioners have filed M.F.A.No.2170/2018.

Heard the arguments of Sri.K.Nagaraja, learned counsel for the KSRTC and Sri Ganapathi,
learned Counsel for the petitioners.
5. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the KSRTC that the Ambika bus was plying from Hosanagar to Shivamogga side.
KSRTC bus was travelling from Shivamogga to Hosanagara side.
There was no occasion for the bus to go to the left side of the road towards Ambika bus and hit against the deceased.
The evidence is placed before the Tribunal to the effect that the deceased in order to go to Bhootharayana temple, has all of a sudden alighted from the Ambika bus, fell down and sustained injuries.
The driver of the KSRTC bus who came from the opposite direction stopped the bus to facilitate first aid to the deceased.
Since there was no insurance to the Ambika bus, FIR is filed against the KSRTC bus for the sake of compensation.
It is further contended that there is no proof of income of the deceased.
Petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are the major sons, they cannot be the dependants NC: 2023:KHC:41050 and excess compensation is awarded and sought for interference.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that the deceased and the group of his villagers were the passengers of the Ambika private bus.
At the place of accident, there was Bhootharayana temple, hence, co-passengers requested the deceased to perform pooja before moving forward.
The deceased after getting down from the Ambika bus, crossed the road, was standing on the left side of the road towards KSRTC bus, at that time, the KSRTC bus hit against the deceased.
The driver of the KSRTC bus has been prosecuted.
It was not challenged either by the driver or the KSRTC.
There are eyewitnesses to the incident, evidence is placed to show non-involvement of Ambika bus.

It is further contended that the deceased was aged 55 years,
Carpenter by avocation and earning Rs.30,000/- per month, but the Tribunal assessed the notional income at Rs.7,000/- without adding future prospects, compensation under the NC:
2023:KHC:41050 conventional heads is on the lower side and sought for enhancement.
7.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of accident, injuries sustained by the deceased, death on account of accidental injuries.
The contention of the KSRTC is that the bus was not involved in the accident.
RW-1/H.Nagaraj is the driver of the bus, RW- 2/K.Chandrappa is the passenger of the KSRTC bus and RW-3/M.Manjunath is the CPI, Hosanagara, who is the Investigating Officer.

On a careful evaluation of the evidence of all these three witnesses, though RWs-1 and 2 disown the accident, the Investigating Officer has made a clear statement before the court on oath about the involvement of the KSRTC bus in the accident and for this reason, the driver was prosecuted for criminal negligence.
During the course of investigation, he has recorded the NC: 2023:KHC:41050 statement of the driver of the Ambika bus and according to him, non-involvement of the said bus is explained.

In the course of cross-examination of RW-3, it is elicited on behalf of the petitioners that where the Ambika bus was parked, no accident has taken place, the accident took place in front of the KSRTC bus.

9. On behalf of the petitioners, the second petitioner, who had accompanied the deceased at the time of accident, on oath has reiterated the manner in which the accident took place; while he and his father were crossing the road, KSRTC bus came and hit against his father injuring him.
The cross-examination of second petitioner has not brought out anything to discredit his worthiness.
PW-2/Arunkumar is the passenger of Ambika bus.
He stands in support of PW-1.
The criminal prosecution is against the driver of the KSRTC bus.
The accident took place at 4.30 p.m. whereas the complaint was filed at 6.30 p.m.
There is no delay in filing the complaint.

If really the deceased while alighting from the Ambika bus fell down,
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41050 there is no chance of he sustaining such a severe head injury.
Photographs are produced on behalf of the KSRTC bus, which clearly point out in favour of the petitioners and will not support the KSRTC.

In the impugned judgment, the Tribunal has evaluated the evidence,
recorded reason in accepting the involvement of the KSRTC bus and non-involvement of Ambika bus.

Hence, the argument deployed on behalf of the KSRTC is not persuasive in nature and it is hard Smt Jayamma vs Nagaraja H L on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156458232/
5 to accept such an argument.

sentences.text: 10. Regarding quantum of compensation is concerned, as referred to supra, the deceased was aged 55 years and he was said to be an agriculturist and carpenter.
The petitioners have produced RTC as per Ex.P17 to show that the deceased is owning 2 acres of land at Kolavalli village of Hosanagara taluk.
Hence, the reason assigned by the Tribunal in assessing notional income of Rs.7,000/- is not acceptable.

Even taking into consideration the fact that in the year 2015 a person with - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:41050 no proof of income will earn not less than Rs.9,000/- per month, the notional income of the deceased has to be accepted at Rs.9,000/-.

11. In a case of this nature, compensation has to be determined by following the principles settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others1 and Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2 so also the principle laid down in Shri Ram General Insurance Co. Ltd. -Vs- Bhagat Singh Rawat & Ors.3 12.

sentences.text: By applying the said principles, the compensation has to be determined.
As rightly argued on behalf of the KSRTC, petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are the major sons, they cannot be treated as dependants.
Hence, the first petitioner alone can be considered as dependant of the deceased.
For the age of 55, applicable multiplier is '11'.
The Tribunal has not considered the future prospects, which ought to have been considered at 10% for the age of 55 years.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation under conventional heads without any rationale.
The deceased was under hospitalization for 14 days.
The medical bills point out a sum of Rs.1,65,000/- has been spent to save the deceased.
That has to be reimbursed.

Taking into consideration the first petitioner as the dependant, the loss of dependency will be: Rs.9,000/- + Rs.900/- (10%)=Rs.9,900/- - Rs.3,300/-(1/3rd) = Rs.6,600/-x12x11 =
Rs.8,71,200/-.
13.

Compensation under the conventional heads has to be determined by following the principles in Pranay Sethi's case (supra), which has been reiterated by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a recent judgment in Bhagat Singh Rawat's case (supra).

Loss of consortium to the wife is at Rs.40,000/-;
love and affection to both sons at Rs.50,000/- together and towards funeral expenses and loss of estate at Rs.15,000/- each, amounting to - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:41050 Rs.1,20,000/-.
Since the claim is of the year 2016, 10% appreciation has to be given for every three years, then it comes to 20% appreciation i.e. Rs.24,000/-.

Then the Smt Jayamma vs Nagaraja H L on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156458232/
6 compensation under conventional heads comes to Rs.1,44,000/- and medical expenses at Rs.1,65,000/-.

sentences.text: The total compensation comes to Rs.11,80,200/- as against Rs.8,41,000/- assessed by the Tribunal.
14. As regards liability is concerned, there is allegation of contributory negligence against the deceased.
As seen from the material on record, the deceased had not sustained any injury while alighting from Ambika bus.
The contention of the petitioner that the deceased was standing on the left side of the road waiting for the second petitioner is also not convincing.
Contrarily, the totality of the evidence did point out that while the KSRTC bus going from the opposite side near Bhootharayana temple, Ambika bus was stopped.
The deceased got down from the bus in a hurry to go to temple to perform pooja, he has all of a sudden crossed the road without noticing the - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:41050 incoming traffic.
If really the petitioner No.2 was accompanying the deceased, he ought to have sustained injuries, but he was inside the Ambika bus.

Hence, the deceased being aged 55 years in a hurry to go to temple abruptly without noticing the incoming traffic crossed the road and thereby he hit against the front portion of the KSRTC bus and sustained severe head injury.
Hence, it is a case of contributory negligence.
15. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, attribution of the deceased is not less than 20%.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled to 80% of the total compensation from the KSRTC.
80% of the total compensation comes to Rs.9,44,160/- as against Rs.8,41,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Then the enhancement comes at Rs.1,03,160/-, which is the just compensation to which the petitioners are entitled.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration.

In the result, the following:
- 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:41050 ORDER (i) Both the appeals are allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified;
(vi) The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records.
